title: Reproducibility Package: A Nutrition-Based Marginal Abatement Cost Curve for Enteric Methane Mitigation in U.S. Dairy Production
description:
Complete reproducibility package for a study constructing a marginal abatement cost curve (MACC) for enteric methane mitigation in U.S. dairy production, using a mechanistically informed, cow-level diet-optimization framework rather than literature-derived engineering assumptions. Includes:

  • Python source code reproducing the full pipeline: dietary NDF reduction (Lever A, constrained nonlinear optimization), 3-nitrooxypropanol supplementation (Lever B, with an explicitly modeled Lever A x B interaction), rumen-available fat supplementation (Lever C), and replacement-rate reduction (Lever D);
  • 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation, including adoption-rate uncertainty in the national-scale scaling exercise;
  • All nine result tables and five figures reported in the accompanying manuscript;
  • Full documentation (codebook, data description, reproducibility checklist, and a step-by-step replication guide).

The study finds that the two most cost-effective levers (dietary NDF reduction and replacement-rate reduction) are cost-saving even without carbon market participation, while a feed additive (3-NOP) and rumen-available fat supplementation are cost-positive; critically, the two most cost-effective levers account for only a small share of the total illustrative national abatement potential identified, demonstrating that cost-effectiveness ranking and abatement-potential ranking are distinct properties of a mitigation portfolio.

This package is organized around the study itself rather than any single journal submission, so that it remains valid regardless of the eventual publication venue or manuscript title.
